To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the European energy industry, the European Union and its member states are in a serious conflict of interest concerning the energy future, and the environmental impacts, of Europe.
the European Union and European corporations are not doing enough to ensure a sustainable energy future for the European Union.
the European energy sector is not ready for the future and it is not ready for sustainability.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: What is the role of the European energy companies in the development of the energy technologies of the future? Do they have any responsibility for the environmental consequences of their business? How do they perceive their responsibility in the field of knowledge production and dissemination? What is the role and position of the energy corporations in the knowledge society?
the question whether the European Union and European energy corporations are able to develop a knowledge based corporate strategy for the sustainable development.

the following questions: What are the corporate strategies of the largest energy corporations of the European Union in the light of the environmental problems of the energy sector? What are the strategies of the European Union concerning sustainable energy? What is the position of the EU and the largest European companies concerning the innovation deficit in the energy sector?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the European energy corporations and the European Union have not yet found the way to a sustainable energy future.

the energy corporations have not yet accepted that their corporate strategies should include a commitment to knowledge production, dissemination and use, which would help to solve the environmental problems caused by their business activities.
the European corporations are not doing enough in the field of knowledge production and dissemination.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the European corporations are not only not doing enough to solve the energy and environmental crisis, but also they are not even trying.

there is a need for a radical change in the way in which the European corporations are managing their knowledge resources, and that there are many reasons to believe that this change is not going to take place without external pressures.
we are not only facing an innovation deficit, but also an ethical deficit of the European energy corporations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the energy sector has to be reformed to become more sustainable and that the energy corporations are not only the main actors, but also the main victims of the energy crisis.
the current corporate strategies are not sustainable and that the European Union should take a more active role in the energy sector in order to achieve its sustainability goals.
the corporate strategies of the largest European energy companies are not consistent with the European Union’s sustainable development policy.
